column1: # boru Language Specification: forward-collection edge cases II —
# per-call-site modifiers, statement-boundary speculation, splice and
# quote interaction, BarrierPos shapes, deep paren nesting.
# Part II of the forward-collection edge matrix (part I: greediness,
# the ONE split rule, barriers, type-directed stopping). Companions:
# §5  Modifiers steer collection PER CALL SITE — /f (all forward),
#     their stacking rules, exercised against the split rule.

column3: /f: both args forward → sig[0]=10, sig[1]=3 → 3-10
…the other operand order
/f pow: 3^2 (sig order unchanged, only the SOURCE of args is pinned)
/f div: 10/2
/f declines the stacked 10: only ONE forward token is there
/f with a single forward arg and no more tokens
/f collects exactly the two it needs; the 3 pushes
same for mul
/s: both from the stack — top 3 → sig[0]
…the other stack order
/s div: top 10 → sig[0], deeper 2 → sig[1] → 2/10 in integer division
…flipped: 10/2
/s with an empty stack: the forward tokens are invisible to it
/s consumes the grouped result and the 5 — nothing reaches forward
/2 removes if's optional else slot: the 42 is NOT collected
…false polarity: no then, no else, the 42 survives
/3 forces the else slot: the 42 IS the else and true discards it
…and false runs it

column1: def n 0 if/2 (n eq 0) [99] def x 1 x
column3: an arity-pinned guard never speculates: no else slot to fill
/2 range: the trailing 2 is free, not a step
/3 range: the 2 is the step
/2 slice picks the (Integer, List) overload
/3 slice consumes exactly three
a redundant /N (pow is only 2-ary) is harmless
/3 selects add's 3-arg (Map, Any, Patrun) shape — which these args cannot fill
/9 names an arity pow does not have
/q yields an Atom: an ordinary VALUE for the next word (3 characters)
the atom's type
atoms of other words are just data too
stacking: q dominates and letters commute
…either spelling
digits stack with f: /f2 ≡ /2f
…either spelling
digits stack with s
f and s are exclusive: a botched modifier is a loud parse error (NUR027)
repeated letters are invalid — same loud error
a NON-alphabet letter keeps the plain-word reading (slash-name), unbound here
/u reverses the call: pow 3 2
/u div: 2/10
/u sub: sub 3 10
/u composes with the mixed split: the reversed sub sees (3, 10) swapped

column1: # §6  Statement-boundary commit and speculative fill — the def idiom
#     a word planned into an Any slot, the barrier probe, and the
#     arrival that completes the parked word.

column3: def's value slot plans `add` speculatively; add's result arrives and completes def
the generator idiom: iota's list arrives as x's value
a measuring word as the speculative filler
a paren value needs no speculation: def completes in phase 1

column1: def x (add 1 2) def y (add x 1) y
column3: chained defs: each call is grouped, then bound
the bound value is the arrival itself
range's optional slot stops at the UNBOUND word s: 2-arg completes, then binds

column1: def a 1 def b 2 add a b
column3: plain multi-statement flow — each def commits before the next statement

column1: def g2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a add b] [a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] g2 1 2 def x 5 x
column3: TYPED overloads: the def word prunes the 3-arg form in phase 1 — the 2-arg call completes before parking

column1: def g2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a add b] [a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] g2 1 2 3
column3: …with a third value present the 3-arg form wins

column1: def g2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a add b] [a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] g2 1 def x 5 x
column3: one arg and a word: no 1-arg overload exists, so the typed plan fails loudly

column1: def ga fn [[a:Any b:Any][Any][add a b] [a:Any b:Any c:Any][Any][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] ga 1 2 def x 5 x
column3: ANY overloads park speculatively instead — the barrier probe commits the exact 2-arg form

column1: def ga fn [[a:Any b:Any][Any][add a b] [a:Any b:Any c:Any][Any][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] ga 1 2 3 def x 5 x
column3: …three claimed args commit the 3-arg form

column1: def ga fn [[a:Any b:Any][Any][add a b] [a:Any b:Any c:Any][Any][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] ga 1 def x 5 x
column3: one claimed arg fails the probe: ga cannot commit and `def` is a barrier — the parked ga strands (no wait-through)
a typed native with no smaller overload fails at plan time (mul sibling of the pinned add row)
an Any-slot native waits through the boundary: x's 5 arrives, truthy → false
a stack value claimed as the else is consumed; the next statement then runs intact
the commit scan works inside a paren scope too

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer][List][if (n eq 0) [raise "z"] range 0 n]] f 2
column3: guard inside a fn body committed by a range statement

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer][List][if (n eq 0) [raise "z"] range 0 n]] f 0
column3: …and the raise pre-empts the range

column1: # §7  Splice-bound words and quote in forward positions — data splices
#     expand like the written paren group (f w ≡ f (w)); code splices
#     stay boundary words; quote takes the NAME, not the binding.

column3: a code splice runs Forth-style against the live stack
a data splice fills both of add's forward slots
…and mul's
sub pins the arrival order: sig[0]=2, sig[1]=3 → 3-2
a literal then the spread: add 1 2 fires, the 3 spills
a barrier after the spread call behaves normally

column1: def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] def vs word [2,3] f3 1 vs
column3: mixed literal + spread fills a 3-arg fn in written order
a heterogeneous data splice fills TYPED slots: take 2 [9 8 7]

column1: # (dropped) word-splice + empty-paren before a splice fails to compile (falls back sound); out of corpus for gate purity
# (dropped) word-splice residual reaching an un-inlinable word declines (an open defect the interpreter absorbs); same disposition as :96

column3: …group it to use its result

column1: def inc word [1 add] 1 inc mul 2
column3: a code splice chains with the live stack: (1+1) then *2
/q takes the NAME vs, binding notwithstanding: two characters
quote captures the word as an atom; the literals push untouched
a quoted word is an Atom value
an atom BOUND to a name flows through collection as plain data
quote of a paren marks the paren's VALUE — a no-op on data
quote cannot ferry a splice: the __SP fires inside the paren first

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] quote z
column3: quote as a guard boundary: commit, then capture
prefix + end binds the evaluated list VALUE (no splice)
; spelling of the same
a forward list value-binding EVALUATES the list at def time: dup finds an empty stack
the prefix form evaluates it even earlier — before def ever runs

column1: # §8  BarrierPos in fn signatures — a leading | makes every param
#     stack-only; a mid-list | splits forward-eligible from
#     stack-only. The or/otherwise natives (part I §4b) are the
#     built-in instances of the same mechanism.
def s fn [[| a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] 10 3 s
column3: stack-only fn: top 3 → a, 10 → b → 3-10

column1: def s fn [[| a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] s 10 3
column3: …and it never collects forward: the literals after it are out of reach

column1: def s fn [[| a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] 5 10 3 s
column3: deeper stack values stay untouched

column1: def m fn [[a:Integer | b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] 10 m 3
column3: mixed fn: a collects the forward 3, b takes the stacked 10 → 3-10

column1: def m fn [[a:Integer | b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] 10 3 m
column3: both slots may still fill from the stack

column1: def m fn [[a:Integer | b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] m 3 10
column3: but b never collects forward: the second literal is unreachable

column1: def m fn [[a:Integer | b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] 7 m 3
column3: the mixed shape reads infix: 3-7

column1: # §8b  import — the module id is collected, and everything after it
#      that no overload can use is left alone (structure-first
#      collection; the classic `end` guard still works).

column3: the dotted call after import is a new statement, not an import argument
a following bare String is NOT collected (no viable overload puts one there)
…the explicit end states the same intent
a following plain list is not taken as a rename list
module exports are namespaced: the bare word after import is not a rename, it is undefined
a paren after import runs as its own expression

column1: # §9  Deep nesting — paren groups as forward arguments, groups inside
#     groups, barriers inside groups, and multi-value groups.

column3: two levels of nesting: ((2*3)+4)*5
left-nested chain
right-nested chain
a double-wrapped group is the same barrier
parens collapse to the value
a whole statement inside a group yields its value
a def inside a group binds in the enclosing scope
end works inside a group: (5+1)*2
; works inside a group
a group is a REAL scope: the second group cannot see the first's result
a group as the forward arg, stack fills the rest
…mirrored
trivial groups are just values

column1: def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] f3 (1) (2) (3)
column3: three grouped forward args fill sig order in WRITTEN order

column1: def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] f3 (1) 2 (3)
column3: groups and literals interleave freely
a MULTI-value group collapses into consecutive slots

column1: def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] f3 (1 2) 3
column3: a two-value group fills a and b; the literal fills c

column1: def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] f3 (1 2 3)
column3: one group can supply every slot
nested groups collapse the same way
an if-group as a condition: inner result feeds the outer slot
